items.headline: Warsh Day 22 Silent — 11 Days to FOMC June 16–17; Cleveland PCE Nowcast 4.18%; April CPI 3.8%; Rate Hike Probability Building; Communication Vacuum Acute; T-HUD Passed Committee −10.4%
items.summary: The June 5 morning economic picture is defined by the Warsh communication vacuum entering its most acute phase. Kevin Warsh advances to Day 22 as Federal Reserve Chair without issuing a public statement, interview, or preparatory guidance. The FOMC inaugural meeting is 11 days out (June 16–17). The vacuum is now structurally dangerous: the Cleveland Fed PCE nowcast holds at 4.18% — more than two percentage points above the Fed's 2% target — and the April headline CPI print of 3.8% (reported May 14, Warsh Day 1) established a stickier-than-anticipated inflation baseline. Minneapolis Fed analysis argues tariffs alone cannot explain the rising goods inflation profile, pointing to energy (Brent ~$95 from Hormuz closure), supply-chain disruption, and tariff-on-tariff compound dynamics. No Warsh public framing has addressed this compound inflation picture. Rate hike probability for the June 16–17 meeting is building without a consensus estimate — markets are pricing rate risk off nowcast data alone, with the absence of any Warsh guidance making the June FOMC a binary outcome rather than a signal-to-market continuity exercise. The FOMC April 28-29 minutes (8-4 hold, the most dissent since October 1992) demonstrated that the rate hike faction within the committee is substantial and growing; Warsh's silence does not suppress those dissents. The iShares Fed Outlook 2026 assessment identifies June 16–17 as a credibility test: a hike without guidance would signal a hawkish break from the Powell template; holding without guidance would signal drift. Either path without communication prep is disruptive. The T-HUD FY27 House Appropriations Committee markup passed June 3 at $92.22B, a -10.4% cut from FY26, on a 34-27 party-line vote. The markup confirms the -10.4% draft number and advances the FY27 budget reconciliation into full House floor scheduling. The transit, housing, and construction sectors now have a confirmed federal funding trajectory: materially negative. PIIE's end-2026 scenario — headline CPI exceeding 4% — is the most likely scenario in its June analysis. Reconciliation 2.0 fiscal uncertainty adds H2 2026 growth-model risk; the Senate's 53-46 procedural vote on the DHS/ICE reconciliation package is a legislative track but not a broader fiscal resolution. Q1 GDP revised to 2.0% — above stall but below trend. Brent ~$95 is the deal-constructive floor.

items.headline: WPA House Vote 215-208 June 3 — Bipartisan Rebuke; Senate Cannot Pass; WPA Day 97 Day 7 Past Hard Deadline; Senate Reconciliation DHS/ICE 53-46; Reconciliation 2.0 House Deadlock 29 Days to July 4
items.summary: The dominant domestic thread on June 5 morning is the compound constitutional-legislative stress from the WPA post-deadline drift, the first bipartisan House WPA majority action, and the dual Reconciliation tracks. The WPA House vote of 215-208 on June 3 — four Republicans (Massie, Barrett, Davidson, Fitzpatrick) joining the Democratic caucus — is the first time a war powers resolution on the Iran conflict has cleared either chamber. It directs Trump to end hostilities within 60 days. The operational consequence is limited: the Senate has not reached cloture on a companion measure (Democrats cannot deliver 60 votes; several Republicans who voted procedurally with Democrats have not committed to a final passage vote), and Trump has signaled veto. However, the House passage marks the first concrete bipartisan majority rebuke of the Iran operation and establishes a political precedent that will shape the Senate's next WPA attempt. The WPA constitutional clock advances to Day 97, Day 7 past the hard 90-day deadline — the longest post-deadline stretch in the series — without enforcement action, litigation, or congressional emergency scheduling. The administration's working posture remains that the WPA clock is contingent on deal closure. Each additional day past the hard deadline without response weakens the WPA as an operative constitutional constraint on future executive war powers. The Senate's 53-46 procedural vote opening debate on the DHS/ICE Reconciliation package is a separate legislative track from the House Reconciliation 2.0 comprehensive package. The Senate DHS/ICE package — a narrower enforcement-spending vehicle — is expected to advance through the chamber this week. Its passage does not resolve the House Reconciliation 2.0 deadlock: at least three House Freedom Caucus members remain opposed to the anti-weaponization fund provision, no floor scheduling has been confirmed, and the July 4 delivery deadline is 29 days away. Punchbowl and Politico reporting continues to characterize the anti-weaponization fund opposition as the session's 'first real GOP resistance.' Any Freedom Caucus whip-count movement is a key watch item for the July 4 calendar.

items.summary: Four secondary domestic threads on June 5 morning. First: Iowa Republican gubernatorial primary result confirmed. MAHA-aligned businessman and farmer Zach Lahn defeated Trump-endorsed Rep. Randy Feenstra, 37.8% to 37.0%, in a five-candidate field. This is the first major Trump-backed candidate loss in a statewide primary in the 2026 cycle. The result has multiple signal vectors: agricultural-district dissatisfaction with tariff and farm subsidy policy; MAHA-coalition energy (Make America Healthy Again, aligned with RFK Jr.'s movement) demonstrating primary power beyond the MAGA frame; and consumer stress from energy prices and tariff pass-through translating into insurgent primary energy in exposed rural districts. The Lahn win is a 2026 midterm leading indicator — it will shape vote-whipping calculations in farm-state House districts on Reconciliation 2.0 and future trade legislation. Second: measles school exposure window has 2 days remaining before the June 7 summer dispersal. National cases exceeded 2,000 in late May. Active clusters include the King County transit case identified June 3 and a Central Virginia outbreak. The CIDRAP slowing signal from June 1-3 holds, but June 7 summer dispersal resets the geographic transmission network — if containment is not achieved by June 7, transmission risk becomes mobile and diffuse through summer travel. CDC has warned state and local health departments that additional cases are anticipated as summer travel escalates. RFK Jr. testimony on measles response is drawing mixed Capitol Hill reception. Third: California Governor primary remains active — Becerra, Porter, and Steyer on the Democratic side; Bianco and Hilton on the Republican. California primary outcome shapes the November general election and state leverage in federal Reconciliation negotiations. Fourth: SCOTUS Alabama redistricting challenge rejected in late May — the ruling clarifying state redistricting latitude has downstream effects on 2026 electoral map calculations and will shape House seats going into 2028.

items.headline: Seattle Mayor Wilson Transit Measure — Council Consideration; FIFA World Cup T-8 Lumen Field; Portland Temperate Week Ahead; Sound Transit Board June Capital Session Pending; NIFC-FIFA Co-Response Risk Building
items.summary: Secondary PNW local threads on June 5 morning. First: Seattle Mayor Bruce Wilson's proposal to renew and expand the Seattle Transit Measure — doubling the city transit sales tax — remains in Seattle City Council consideration. The T-HUD FY27 committee passage at -10.4% materially reduces the federal-match offset path for Sound Transit's $34.5B funding gap, making the local measure more urgent. The political path requires ballot approval in a 2026 election year, with the economic context of elevated consumer stress from energy prices and tariff pass-through complicating the calculus for a regressive consumption tax increase. Sound Transit's board is expected to address the gap in its June capital planning session; the T-HUD committee number will be a material input. Second: FIFA World Cup Seattle is T-8 from this morning — first match at Lumen Field on June 13, continuing through July 7. DHS-Secret Service security coordination is active. The NIFC above-normal fire condition creates a growing co-risk scenario: if a significant fire ignites in the east Cascades or Columbia Gorge during the FIFA window, emergency response resources — air assets, personnel, evacuation routes — face competing demands with mass-event security and visitor transportation. Portland-area transportation planners have flagged this concern in coordination calls with Oregon OEM. Third: Portland is forecast to be temperate this week — high 60s to low 70s after the late May heat advisory (92°F on June 1). The cooling provides a brief firefighting fuel moisture reprieve on west-side slopes before seasonal drying resumes. The next significant heat window is not forecast before late June. The temperate forecast supports air quality for the FIFA pre-tournament preparation period in the Seattle corridor. Fourth: Oregon's PNW drought stress continues with the south Cascades extreme classification forecasting a compressed, high-intensity ignition season when temperature reversals arrive in July. The east Cascades onset timeline — unchanged at July — is the primary local infrastructure co-risk for the FIFA window.

analyst_summary: June 5, 2026 morning opens at Vibe 3 — consistent with the June 4 evening close but with a materially altered threat distribution. The central organizing tension has bifurcated: the Iran-US deal channel is confirmed open (comms resolved Day 1 morning, no overnight re-suspension signal), but the Lebanon track has deteriorated sharply overnight with Hezbollah's formal rejection of the full ceasefire framework. The morning's primary constructive hold is the Iran comms confirmation: the June 2-4 suspension cycle is resolved without re-triggering, and both sides remain in active engagement. The morning's primary new stress is Lebanon: Hezbollah leader Kassem's June 4 characterization of the full framework as 'absurd, humiliating, and insulting' dismantles the full Lebanon ceasefire architecture and leaves the Beirut-suburbs partial truce as the only operative de facto agreement. That partial truce entered Day 3 overnight clean — the absence of Dahiyeh strikes and Hezbollah attacks on Israel is the morning's primary constructive Lebanon data point — but the Hezbollah rejection removes the political ceiling on escalation. The Lebanon-Iran comms linkage remains the operational hairline fracture: any Israeli action that Hezbollah treats as a trigger could cascade into comms re-suspension within hours. The WPA House vote (215-208, June 3) is the domestic constitutional development of the week — the first bipartisan House majority action against the Iran operation, carried by four Republicans. Its operational consequence is limited (Senate cloture path unavailable, Trump veto likely), but it demonstrates that the WPA post-deadline drift at Day 97 (Day 7 past the hard 90-day constitutional deadline) is generating bipartisan political consequence even without enforcement. Iowa's Lahn win over Trump-backed Feenstra is the cycle's first major Trump primary loss — a MAHA-agricultural-tariff confluence that signals insurgent primary energy in exposed rural districts with downstream implications for 2026 midterm vote-whipping. The T-HUD committee passage at -10.4% confirms the negative federal funding trajectory for transit and housing. Five structural stresses advancing unchanged: WPA Day 97 (no enforcement, no litigation, no congressional scheduling); Reconciliation 2.0 House anti-weaponization deadlock (3+ Freedom Caucus holdouts, 29 days to July 4); Warsh Day 22 silent (11 days to inaugural FOMC, Cleveland nowcast 4.18%, rate hike probability building, communication vacuum acute); NIFC above-normal Day 5 (east Cascades drying advancing, July onset unchanged, no overnight ignitions); measles 2 days to June 7 school dispersal (summer transmission network at dispersal edge). Today's actionable watchlist is organized around five triggers: any Trump or Khamenei MOU formal endorsement (Day 8 dual-principal gap; signing shifts to Vibe 4-5); Hezbollah or Israel action breaking the Dahiyeh partial truce (immediate Lebanon escalation = Iranian comms re-suspension risk = Vibe 2); Brent trading below $93 sustained (deal conviction building) or above $107 (credibility collapse); Warsh any pre-FOMC public statement (11 days out; any signal is market-moving); Reconciliation 2.0 Freedom Caucus whip-count movement (29 days to July 4). PNW local stress is at its most acute compound window: NIFC Day 5, 82% Oregon drought, extreme south Cascades, complete snowpack melt, east Cascades July onset, FIFA co-response risk building from T-8. Vibe 3 holds. The upgrade path to 4 is specific: MOU formally endorsed by Trump and Khamenei with Hormuz reopening timeline confirmed; OR Hezbollah re-engages with a fifth Washington round. The downgrade path to 2 is also specific: Iranian comms re-suspension (any Israeli action beyond south Lebanon as trigger); Hezbollah attacks Israel breaking the Dahiyeh partial truce; CENTCOM repositioning or kinetic action.
